entities.name: PMID:25086730
observations: 2014 systematic review of weight training in women with breast-cancer-related lymphoedema; included 11 reports from 8 randomized trials involving 1,091 women.
Included supervised, gradually progressed low-to-moderate weight training; all trials used pressure garments and no trial tested high-intensity lifting.
Established lymphoedema arm-volume change did not worsen: SMD −0.09, 95% CI −0.23 to 0.05; incidence in at-risk women was not increased: RR 0.77, 95% CI 0.52 to 1.15.

entities.name: PMID:31406873
observations: 2019 systematic review of weight-lifting or resistance exercise for breast-cancer-related lymphoedema; included 15 papers comprising 13 resistance-only and 2 combined resistance-aerobic trials.

In established lymphoedema, six studies found no significant swelling difference and three reported greater arm-volume reduction with resistance exercise; in at-risk women, six studies reported no exercise-caused lymphoedema or adverse events.
The review noted small samples and heterogeneous evidence, despite included studies having PEDro scores of 7–10.

entities.name: Breast cancer-related lymphoedema
observations: The reviewed evidence concerns established lymphoedema after breast-cancer treatment and prevention of lymphoedema in women at risk.

entities.name: Supervised resistance training
observations: Gradual, supervised low-to-moderate resistance or weight training appears not to worsen established breast-cancer-related lymphoedema or increase its onset in at-risk women.
Evidence does not establish safety for unsupervised, rapidly progressed, heavy, or high-intensity lifting.

entities.name: No demonstrated lymphoedema harm
observations: Across the identified systematic reviews, appropriately supervised and gradually progressed resistance training showed no demonstrated increase in arm volume, worsening of established lymphoedema, or onset in at-risk women.
